h
and its ḍuḥā

they denied him and hamstrung her

, when the people, before the killing of the she-camel, had conceded to her a day's drinking and to themselves a day's drinking on another day?” It is said: The report has come that after conceding that they agreed together to prevent her from drinking and were content with her being killed; and it was with the consent of all of them that her killer killed her and whoever hamstrung her hamstrung her; and for that reason the denial and the hamstringing were attributed to all of them, so He, majestic is His praise, said:
h
But they denied him and hamstrung her
And His saying:
h
So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and levelled it
. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: So their Lord destroyed
n
them, [and that was]
n
because of their disbelief in Him, their denial of His messenger Ṣāliḥ, and their hamstringing of His she-camel;
h
and levelled it
. He says: So He made the destruction level upon all of them, and none of them escaped.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and levelled it
: It was mentioned to us that the Uḥaymir of Thamūd refused to hamstring her until her young and old,
and her females, had pledged themselves to him; and when the people shared in hamstringing her, God brought down upon them destruction for their sin and levelled it

c: Bishr b. Ādam told me, he said:
m: Qutaybah told us, he said: Abū Hilāl told us, he said: I heard al-Ḥasan say: When they hamstrung the she-camel, they sought her foal, and it went into the qārah of the mountain, so God cut their hearts

x: And His saying:
h
And He does not fear its consequence
The people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning; some of them said: its meaning is: God does not fear the consequence of His bringing destruction upon them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiyah told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: And He does not fear its consequence
. He said: God does not fear a reckoning from anyone

c: Ibrāhīm b. al-Mustamirr told me, he said:
m: told us, he said: ʿUmar b. Mazīd
told us, from al-Ḥasan, on His saying:
And He does not fear its consequence
. He said: That is our Lord, blessed and exalted; He does not fear from them

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us,
m: b. Munabbih—Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī said: this is how it is in my copy—he said: I heard al-Ḥasan recite:
And He does not fear its consequence
. He said: That is the Lord; He did that to them and did not fear a reckoning.

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan,
m: And He does not fear its consequence
. He said: He does not fear their reckoning.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: And He does not fear its consequence
. He says: He does not fear being called to account for any of what He did to them

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His saying:
And He does not fear its consequence
. Muḥammad b. ʿAmr said in his report: God does not fear its consequence. And al-Ḥārith said in his report: God does not fear its consequence

c: Muḥammad b. Sinān told me, he said: Yaʿqūb told us, he said:
m: told us, he said: I heard Bakr b. ʿAbdallāh al-Muzanī say, on His saying:
And He does not fear its consequence
. He said: God does not fear a reckoning.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: and the one who hamstrung her did not fear its consequence, that is, the consequence of the deed he did.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Jābir b. Nūḥ told us, he said: Abū Rawq told us, he said: al-Ḍaḥḥāk told us:
m: And He does not fear its consequence
. He said: The one who hamstrung her did not fear its consequence

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from al-Suddī:
m: And He does not fear its consequence
: The one who did it does not fear the consequence of what he did
. The reciters differed in the reading of this: the generality of the reciters of the Ḥijāz and Syria read: (fa-lā yakhāfu ʿuqbāhā) with the fāʾ
, and likewise it is in their copies of the muṣḥaf
. The generality of the reciters of Iraq, in the two cities, read it with the wāw:

, and likewise it is in their copies of the muṣḥaf (4). The correct view on this is that they are two well-known readings, not differing in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct. The reciters also differed on the imālah of those words in this sūrah and others that are of the wāw-type; that is like His saying
And [by] the moon when it follows it
And [by] the earth and He who spread it

, and the like of that; the generality of the reciters of Kūfah would pronounce all of that with fatḥ, and they would incline (imālah) those that are of the yāʾ-type, except ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī; for ʿĀṣim would pronounce all of that with fatḥ, both what was of the wāw-type and what was of the yāʾ-type, not inclining
any of it. And al-Kisāʾī would incline all of that

. And Abū ʿAmr would look at the evenness of the verse-endings: if they were consistent in one thing, he would incline all of them. As for the generality of the reciters of Medina, they do not incline any of that with strong imālah, nor do they open it with a strong fatḥ, but something in between
. And the most eloquent and best of that is to look to the beginning of the sūrah: if the verse-endings are with yāʾ, all of them are treated with imālah that is not excessive

; and if the verse-endings are with wāw, they are opened and all treated with a fatḥ that is not excessive; and when one type occurs singly in a place, the yāʾ-type are inclined with moderate imālah and the wāw-type are pronounced with a medium fatḥ; and if the former are inclined and the others opened, it would not be a solecism, except that the eloquent form of speech is what we have described. End of the commentary on Sūrat “Wa-l-shamsi wa-ḍuḥāhā”.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of this: the generality of the reciters of the Ḥijāz and Syria read: (fa-lā yakhāfu ʿuqbāhā) with the fāʾ (3), and likewise it is in their copies of the muṣḥaf (4).
The generality of the reciters of Iraq, in the two cities, read it with the wāw: {wa-lā yakhāfu ʿuqbāhā} (5), and likewise it is in their copies of the muṣḥaf (4).

The reciters also differed on the imālah of those words in this sūrah and others that are of the wāw-type; that is like His saying {And [by] the moon when it follows it}, {And [by] the earth and He who spread it}, and the like of that; the generality of the reciters of Kūfah would pronounce all of that with fatḥ, and they would incline (imālah) those that are of the yāʾ-type, except ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī; for ʿĀṣim would pronounce all of that with fatḥ, both what was of the wāw-type and what was of the yāʾ-type, not inclining (6) any of it.
As for the generality of the reciters of Medina, they do not incline any of that with strong imālah, nor do they open it with a strong fatḥ, but something in between (8).

notes.en: Al-qāra is a small hill. Tāj al-ʿarūs, root (ق و ر). A similar report appeared above, 10/295, through ʿAbd al-Razzāq from Maʿmar from someone who heard al-Ḥasan.
notes.ar: القارة: الجُبَيْل الصغير. التاج (ق و ر). والأثر تقدم تخريجه بنحوه في 10/ 295 من طريق عبد الرزاق، عن معمر، عمن سمع الحسن.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim (as cited in al-Itqān, 2/56) reported it through Abū Ṣāliḥ. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to Khushaysh in al-Istiqāma and Ibn al-Mundhir, 6/357.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في الإتقان 2/ 56 - من طريق أبى صالح به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 357 إلى خشيش في الاستقامة وابن المنذر.

notes.en: S, M, T1, T2, and T3 read “ʿAmr.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 2/202.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "عمرو". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 2/ 202.

notes.en: The original reads “Yazīd”; S, M, and T1 read “Murthid.” See al-Tārīkh al-kabīr, 6/197, and al-Jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl, 6/135.
notes.ar: في الأصل: "يزيد"، وفى ص، م، ت 1: "مرثد". وينظر التاريخ الكبير 6/ 197، والجرح والتعديل 6/ 135.

notes.en: Omitted from S, M, T1, T2, and T3.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3.

notes.en: M reads “from what.”
notes.ar: في م: "مما".

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to al-Muṣannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, 6/357.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 357 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وعبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: S, M, T1, T2, and T3 read “ʿAmr.” He is ʿUmar ibn Mazīd in the preceding chain; al-Bukhārī says there that Wakīʿ called him ʿUmar ibn Munabbih.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "عمرو". وهو عمر بن مزيد الذي في الإسناد قبله، وقد نص البخارى في الموضع السابق أن وكيعا هو الذي سماه عمر بن منبه.

notes.en: Its source references were given above, p. 449.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في ص 449.

notes.en: Its source references were given above, p. 447.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في ص 447.

notes.en: The original reads “Razīn Abū Sulaymān”; S “Razīn Ibrāhīm from Abū Sulaymān”; M “Razīn ibn Ibrāhīm from Abū Sulaymān”; T1, T2, T3 “Razīn Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Sulaymān.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "رزين أبى سليمان"، وفى ص: "رزين إبراهيم عن أبي سليمان"، وفى م: "رزين بن إبراهيم عن أبي سليمان"، وفى ت 1، ت 2 ت 3: "رزين إبراهيم بن أبى سليمان".

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to al-Muṣannaf, 6/357.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 357 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: S, M, T1, and T2 add: “He does not fear the consequence of the one who hamstrung her. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us … from al-Suddī: ‘He does not fear its consequence’ means the one who …”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2: "لم يخف الذي عقرها عقباها. حدثنا ابن حميد قال ثنا مهران عن سفيان عن السدى: {ولا يخاف عقباها} قال: الذي".

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to al-Muṣannaf and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, 6/357.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 357 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: This is the reading of Nāfiʿ, Abū Jaʿfar, and Ibn ʿĀmir. Al-Nashr, 2/300.
notes.ar: وهى قراءة نافع وأبى جعفر وابن عامر. النشر 2/ 300.

notes.en: See Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān by Abū ʿUbayd, pp. 197, 199, and Ibn Abī Dāwūd’s al-Maṣāḥif, pp. 40, 47.
notes.ar: ينظر فضائل القرآن لأبى عبيد ص 197، 199، والمصاحف لابن أبي داود ص 40، 47.

notes.en: This is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Yaʿqūb, and Khalaf. Al-Nashr, 2/300.
notes.ar: وهى قراءة ابن كثير وأبى عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائى ويعقوب وخلف. النشر 2/ 300.

notes.en: The original and T1 read “he opens”; S “he reclines”; T2 and T3 “she reclines.” The meaning is that he does not incline.
notes.ar: في الأصل، ت 1: "يفتح"، وفى ص: "يضطجع"، وفى ت 2، ت 3: "تضجع". والمعنى: أنه لا يميل.

notes.en: That is, he applies strong imāla, bringing the vowel close to kasra.
notes.ar: أي: يميل إمالة كبرى قريبة من الكسر.

notes.en: The readers differ on imāla at the verse endings in Sūrat al-Shams. Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf apply strong imāla to all endings except “it followed it” and “its morning brightness.”
notes.ar: القراء منقسمون في إمالة رءوس الآى من سورة الشمس؛ فقد قرأ حمزة والكسائى وخلف بإمالة =

notes.en: Abū ʿAmr applies taqlīl to all endings; Warsh from Nāfiʿ uses intermediate imāla; the others read with fatḥ alone.
notes.ar: = رءوس الآى إمالة كبرى ما عدا {تَلَاهَا} و {ضُحَاهَا}. وقرأ أبو عمرو بتعليل رءوس الآى جميعها، وقرأ ورش عن نافع بالإمالة بَيْن بَيْن. وقرأ الباقون بالفتح قولًا واحدًا.

notes.en: That is, without making it as strong as kasra.
notes.ar: أي: غير المبالغ فيها نحو الكسر.

notes.en: The original reads “amīlā.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "أميلا".

notes.en: T1, T2, and T3 read “the correct reading.”
notes.ar: في ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "الصحيح".
